segment_text: 8.3 Third Party Fees and Royalties. Bellicum will reimburse Miltenyi for Third Party royalties and/or license fees, if any, owed by Miltenyi under Third Party license agreements existing as of the Effective Date as set forth on Exhibit D solely to the extent Miltenyi's exercise of rights under such licenses is required 27 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) to supply Miltenyi Product to Bellicum under this Agreement for the Permitted Use; and further provided that amounts owed under such Third Party license agreements have not otherwise been passed through to Bellicum and are actually paid by Miltenyi to Miltenyi's licensor(s). Bellicum acknowledges that the potential volume of such Third Party royalties and/or license fees under applicable Third Party license agreements will be as set forth on Exhibit D, as updated from time to time by Miltenyi. If, during the Term of this Agreement, the Parties mutually agree to obtain additional Third Party licenses to enable the Permitted Use of Miltenyi Products by Bellicum, its Affiliates, Subcontractors, and/or Licensees under this Agreement, and such additional licenses give rise to Third Party royalties and/or license fees with respect to Bellicum's use of Miltenyi Products under this Agreement, then the Parties will negotiate in good faith which Party(ies) is/are responsible for payment of such Third Party royalties and/or license fees. Miltenyi, acting reasonably, reserves the right to defer the inclusion of additional Miltenyi Products in Exhibit B hereto until the Parties have reached agreement on this matter.

§14.4 DRAFTING SESSION, 2026-09-16. Eligibility was RULED BY THE REVIEWER at v0.52 (§10.2, SPLITTING_EXCLUSION_INVESTIGATION.md Decision 3); this session drafts the item and resolves the §8.8 question that ruling deliberately left open. The segment disposition moves PENDING_ANNOTATION -> ANNOTATED, and C04-117 now reconciles fully at 3 items for 3 obligation-bearing clauses.

ACTION -- §8.8'S DECISION PROCEDURE WAS RUN EXPLICITLY. The real verb is "defer", recorded verbatim here as §8.8 requires. RULED A GENUINE GAP: action = WITHHOLD (the nearest member), action_accept_set = ["WITHHOLD"] alone per §8.8's single-verb requirement, known_gaps gains action_not_in_taxonomy. The full measurement is the new §8.8.3; in short, `ACTIONS` holds no DEFER/POSTPONE/SUSPEND (checked by execution -- cold's DEFER/WITHHOLD/SUSPEND set held exactly one legal verb and was not lockable), and WITHHOLD is nearest by appearance but is NOT the same performance. All 41 withhold-family sentences in the 1,547-segment pool keep back something OWED, DUE or REQUESTED -- consent/approval (~24), tax deducted from a payment (~9, including §8.8's own `deduct`->WITHHOLD worked case at C14-076), or a payment/delivery/document held back (~8). Not one postpones a step that is not yet due. Miltenyi's deferral keeps back nothing owed: no duty to include additional Products in Exhibit B exists, which is exactly what the Parties have yet to agree. §8.8.2's discriminators both fire AFFIRMATIVELY: the corpus's own boilerplate enumerates withholding and delaying as separately failable in 10 of the 41 sentences (24.4%) across 5 documents -- "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed" -- which is the same evidence shape as §8.8.2's "failed to defend or indemnify"; and deferral carries an END-POINT that withholding does not. Labelling this WITHHOLD would assert that inclusion WAS due and is being kept back -- the OVERSTATING direction §9.1 ground 2 names as a validity failure.

AN ARGUMENT FOR MAPPING THAT WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, recorded so it is not reinvented: one could say nothing is lost because the deferral's temporal content is carried by this item's own `temporal` field. That is unsound -- it makes an `action` ruling depend on another field's content for one item, so a bare "may defer" with no end-point would decide the same verb the opposite way. §8.8 asks about the verb.

STATED AGAINST INTEREST: "defer" occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the whole 1,547-segment pool -- this sentence. There is no base rate for it and none is claimed; the 41-sentence measurement is of WITHHOLD, the member being mapped onto, which is the side the same-performance test needs.

DENOMINATOR -- CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION RATHER THAN ASSUMED, as this segment's v0.52 drafting_instructions required. known_gaps holds TWO tags and EITHER alone keeps this item out of §9.1's in-force criterion-2 denominator: relative_trigger_preposition (the temporal call, see below) and action_not_in_taxonomy (the ruling above). So the §8.8 answer does not move the in-force figure for THIS item, unlike its sibling C11-02 where it was decisive. The item does enter the all-items denominator once scoreable.

Under §6's modal rule the outcome is MISSED. The emitted verb DEFER is off-taxonomy and fails clause 2 regardless of this ruling.

MODALITY MAY per §3.2's "is entitled to / is permitted to" row -- "reserves the right to" is an entitlement. §3.3 forbids an accept-set. §2.5.1 is explicit that the modal decides modality but not eligibility, and eligibility here was settled separately: three independent monitorable stakes, reached concordantly by two independent annotators in the same order -- a REVIEWABLE standard ("acting reasonably", §2.5.1's own counter-example to "sole business judgment"), a bounded observable end-point ("until the Parties have reached agreement"), and a narrow specific object, against C04-026's unrestricted ten-verb catch-all and distinguished from §2.5.1's C14-044 negative example. Per §7.1 that concordance is a LOWER BOUND on error, not proof: correlated model-family error, guideline leakage and no reviewer blinding all apply.

OBJECT_CLASS. The object phrase "the inclusion of additional Miltenyi Products in Exhibit B hereto" has two nominal anchors, so §3.6's REQUIRED enumeration 1 demands both: the act-noun anchor (product_inclusion, exhibit_inclusion) and the thing anchor (additional_products, miltenyi_products), plus product_listing. Five entries, inside the 3-6 band. Cold's set carried both "additional_products" and "additional_product", which §3.6 forbids in terms -- "Number is NOT one of these enumerations. Do not pad a set with plurals", since §5 clause 5 normalizes number on both sides as of v0.33 -- so the padded duplicate is dropped and miltenyi_products takes the slot instead. §3.6.1 CHECKED rather than waved through, because "inclusion" is an act-nominalisation and could look like a restatement of `action`: it is not, on two independent grounds -- this item's action is WITHHOLD/defer, not "include", so no field co-varies; and carve-out 1 covers it anyway, since "the inclusion" is the head of the object's own noun phrase in the span.

TEMPORAL -- RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER(before, "the Parties have reached agreement on this matter"), trigger verbatim, known_gaps gains relative_trigger_preposition. §8.9's v0.34 data correction is the governing authority and it is explicit that "until" was never counted but IS covered by the rule as written, expressing a `before` direction; that same correction records "until <trigger>" occurring in C04-117 twice, which is this sentence. Cross-checked against §8.6.1 (v0.52) as the drafting_instructions required: its unifying principle -- null marks what the IR cannot REPRESENT, never what the classifier cannot REACH -- now governs both preposition gaps identically, and confirms annotating the form here rather than null. Expected v1 outcome is UNMAPPABLE_TEMPORAL, a LOUD failure visible in criterion 1b, per §8.9 and §15.3.1.

MISSING_FIELDS USES "temporal.trigger", NOT "temporal" -- a CORRECTION to the cold draft, verified against the production code rather than copied. compiler/typecheck.py's _typecheck_temporal appends the path "temporal.trigger" for the RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER form (the `_resolve_trigger(temporal.trigger, "temporal.trigger", ...)` call), and locked item C11-01 already uses that spelling. §3.9 trigger 3 fires regardless, since symbols.resolve_trigger() returns None throughout v1. §5's predicate does not read missing_fields (§10.1 F15), so this does not move a score -- it is recorded correctly because the field is meant to predict what the pipeline actually produces.

CONDITIONS -- EMPTY, deliberately. "acting reasonably" is a STANDARD governing how the right may be exercised, not an if-type circumstance on which the permission depends; it is §2.5.1's reviewable-standard discriminator and does the eligibility work recorded above, not condition work. "until the Parties have reached agreement on this matter" is the temporal, not a condition. No §3.8.3 restatement, so no conditions_accept_set.
